assets.title: Alexander the Great
assets.subtitle: King of Macedon
assets.bodyText: King of Macedon from 336 to 323 BCE, Alexander overthrew the Persian Empire and led his army into India. His conquests reshaped the ancient world and opened the Hellenistic age.

sources.title: The Rise of Macedon and the Conquests of Alexander the Great — Metropolitan Museum of Art

assets.title: Campaign Soldier
assets.subtitle: In the King's Ranks
assets.bodyText: A campaign soldier drills with spear and shield, keeps equipment ready, and holds position beside the rest of the unit. Dependable service under orders lays the foundation for the judgment and responsibility of command.
assets.sceneBrief: An adult Macedonian campaign soldier practising formation with spear and shield beside fellow soldiers; practical equipment, no messenger dispatch or stores duties.

assets.title: Campaign Squad Leader
assets.subtitle: Steadying a Small Command
assets.bodyText: A campaign squad leader directs a small group of soldiers on the march and in the field. Clear instructions, shared discipline, and care for the unit turn individual service into the first responsibility of command.
assets.sceneBrief: An adult small-unit leader gives clear directions to a few equipped Macedonian campaign soldiers; a modest field command, not a granary or provisioner scene.

assets.bodyText: A staff officer turns reports, routes, and supply figures into decisions the army can trust. Close to the command tent, careful judgment keeps scattered forces aligned with Alexander's astonishing ambition.

assets.title: Aristotle
assets.subtitle: Philosopher of the Lyceum
assets.bodyText: Aristotle made inquiry a life's work, examining logic, ethics, politics, and the living world. At the Lyceum in Athens, his investigations helped establish enduring ways to observe, classify, and reason.

sources.title: Aristotle — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
Aristotle's Biology — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

assets.title: Lyceum Student
assets.subtitle: First Questions of the Lyceum
assets.bodyText: A Lyceum student records questions, studies arguments, and checks simple observations with the school. Careful notes and a willingness to test an explanation begin the habits that later support independent research and teaching.
assets.sceneBrief: An adult student records questions and simple observations while learning in the Lyceum; introductory inquiry rather than general courier work.

assets.bodyText: A copyist preserves arguments with a steady hand, protecting distinctions that careless writing could erase. The work carries a lesson beyond the speaker's voice, giving the Lyceum's inquiry a lasting memory.

assets.title: Euclid
assets.subtitle: Geometer of Alexandria
assets.bodyText: Euclid's Elements organized geometry and number into a powerful sequence of definitions, propositions, and proofs. Associated with Alexandria, this elusive mathematician gave generations a model of knowledge built through reason.

sources.title: Euclid — MacTutor, University of St Andrews
Who was Euclid? — Princeton University Press

assets.title: Geometry Apprentice
assets.subtitle: Learner of the First Principles
assets.bodyText: A geometry apprentice learns to draw a circle and name what a figure contains. Small acts of precision begin a greater discipline, turning a curious eye toward the certainty of proof.
assets.sceneBrief: A young adult apprentice draws one simple circle with dividers on a wax tablet or sand board, plain linen, modest courtyard.

assets.title: Lysippos
assets.subtitle: Master Sculptor of Sikyon
assets.bodyText: A celebrated sculptor from Sikyon, Lysippos worked chiefly in bronze and portrayed Alexander the Great. His lost originals survive through ancient testimony and later copies, preserving the influence of an extraordinary workshop.

sources.title: Lysippos — Getty Union List of Artist Names
Power and Pathos: exhibition checklist — J. Paul Getty Museum

assets.title: Workshop Apprentice
assets.subtitle: At the Sculptor's Bench
assets.bodyText: A workshop apprentice prepares clay, tends tools, and watches experienced hands shape a figure. Familiarity with the material slowly becomes judgment, laying the humble foundation from which convincing bronze can rise.
assets.sceneBrief: A simply dressed workshop apprentice prepares clay or wax at a low bench, bronze casting workshop behind, no master portrait pose.

assets.bodyText: A master sculptor unites proportion, gesture, and command of bronze into a figure that seems alive. Such judgment carries the workshop's tradition forward, making technical mastery serve an unmistakable human presence.

assets.title: Pytheas of Massalia
assets.subtitle: Explorer of the Northern Seas
assets.bodyText: An explorer from Massalia, Pytheas described Britain and the distant north in a work now lost. Later writers preserve fragments of his observations, leaving a remarkable voyage whose route remains debated.

sources.title: Pytheas — Oxford Dictionary of National Biography
Pytheas of Massalia — Encyclopedia of Ancient History

assets.title: Deckhand of Massalia
assets.subtitle: Crew of the Northern Venture
assets.bodyText: A deckhand handles rope, cargo, and the small repairs that keep a vessel ready. Steady labour gives the expedition its footing, making the next unfamiliar coast possible long before it appears.
assets.sceneBrief: A common deckhand coils hemp rope aboard a simple Massaliot merchant vessel; coarse tunic, harbour or calm sea, no elite equipment.

assets.title: Menander
assets.subtitle: Master of New Comedy
assets.bodyText: Menander made Athenian New Comedy a theatre of recognisable lives, misunderstandings, and uneasy relationships. His plays shaped later comic drama, giving ordinary human motives a place beside the grand stories of heroes.

sources.title: Menander — Oxford Classical Dictionary
Menander: author, transmission, and text — Dickinson College Commentaries

assets.title: Rehearsal Assistant
assets.subtitle: Learning the Comic Stage
assets.bodyText: A rehearsal assistant follows scene copies, records cues, and helps the company try a comic exchange in performance. Attention to dialogue and timing gives early practice in the dramatic work that will grow into writing and staging.
assets.sceneBrief: An adult rehearsal assistant follows a scene copy and records performance cues beside a New Comedy company.

assets.title: Demetrius the Besieger
assets.subtitle: King of Siegecraft
assets.bodyText: Demetrius Poliorcetes pursued kingship through bold campaigns and spectacular siege machinery. His famous assault on Rhodes ended in negotiation, yet its scale fixed his enduring reputation as the Besieger of Cities.

sources.title: Demetrius I of Macedonia, Poliorcetes — Oxford Classical Dictionary
The Great Siege of Rhodes — Oxford University Press

assets.title: Siege Labourer
assets.subtitle: Hand of the Siege Train
assets.bodyText: A siege labourer moves timber, rope, and stone where the builders need them. Endurance turns the engineer's design into solid material, raising the patient groundwork beneath a machine meant to challenge walls.
assets.sceneBrief: A plain-clothed siege labourer carries timber or coils of heavy rope at a construction yard, unfinished timber tower behind; no advanced engineering instruments.

assets.bodyText: A workshop assistant shapes fittings and checks the ropes that larger engines depend upon. Exact preparation keeps immense forces under control, making the smallest sound component a quiet ally against the strongest wall.

assets.title: Theophrastus
assets.subtitle: Scholar of the Living World
assets.bodyText: Aristotle's colleague and successor at the Lyceum, Theophrastus explored philosophy and the natural world. His surviving botanical treatises gathered and compared plant knowledge, establishing a foundation for the systematic study of plants.

sources.title: Theophrastus — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

assets.title: Garden Attendant
assets.subtitle: Tending the Scholar's Garden
assets.bodyText: A garden attendant waters specimens and notices the small changes of another growing day. Patient care keeps living examples within reach, giving the school's larger questions roots in plants that can be observed.
assets.sceneBrief: A modest garden attendant waters or tends several plant specimens in a Greek courtyard garden; simple tunic, no master scholar's collection of instruments.

assets.title: Zeno of Citium
assets.subtitle: Founder of the Stoa
assets.bodyText: Teaching at Athens' Painted Porch, Zeno founded the Stoic school around 300 BCE. His philosophy placed virtue and reason at the centre of a demanding vision of how a life should be lived.

sources.title: Stoicism — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

assets.title: Listener at the Stoa
assets.subtitle: First Steps Beside Zeno
assets.bodyText: A listener beneath the porch gives a difficult argument the attention it deserves. Honest willingness to reconsider an easy answer marks the first small victory of reason over habit.
assets.sceneBrief: A plainly dressed adult listener beside the painted colonnade holds a simple wax tablet, thoughtful attentive gaze; not posed as the school's teacher.

assets.title: Ptolemy I Soter
assets.subtitle: Founder of a Dynasty
assets.bodyText: A general of Alexander, Ptolemy secured Egypt after the conqueror's death and later ruled as king. His dynasty made Alexandria a royal capital and endured until the age of Cleopatra.

sources.title: Ptolemy I Soter — Digital Egypt, University College London

assets.subtitle: Learning the Court's Accounts
assets.bodyText: A court records apprentice copies entries, checks names and quantities, and helps reconcile the day's administrative papers. Precise records are the first practical lesson in the wider duties of supply, revenue, and government.
assets.sceneBrief: An adult court records apprentice carries and checks administrative papers in an early Ptolemaic office.

assets.title: Cleomenes of Naucratis
assets.subtitle: Financier of Alexander's Egypt
assets.bodyText: Appointed by Alexander to administer Egyptian revenue, Cleomenes became a powerful financial official. His control of grain and taxation amassed wealth, while ancient accounts also preserve accusations of ruthless exploitation and profiteering.

sources.title: Cleomenes of Naucratis — Oxford Classical Dictionary

assets.title: Steward of Egyptian Grain Accounts
assets.subtitle: Keeper of the Harvest Reckoning
assets.bodyText: A senior grain steward reconciles reports from granaries, markets, and transport routes into one accountable picture. Command of the whole system makes this office a powerful guardian of Egypt's reserves and obligations.

assets.title: Nearchus
assets.subtitle: Admiral of Alexander's Fleet
assets.bodyText: Nearchus commanded Alexander's fleet from the Indus towards the Persian Gulf. His account of the difficult coastal voyage, preserved through later writers, joined practical seamanship to an enduring record of unfamiliar shores.

sources.title: Arrian, Indica — Fordham University Ancient History Sourcebook
Arrian on Nearchus' voyage home — Livius

assets.title: Fleet Deckhand
assets.subtitle: Crew of Nearchus' Ships
assets.bodyText: A fleet deckhand tends lines, stows gear, and answers the work of another tide. Dependable hands keep the vessel ready for orders, giving the admiral's distant destination a practical beginning on deck.
assets.sceneBrief: A humble fleet deckhand tends rigging on an ancient expedition ship, simple working tunic, salt-worn rope, coastal water behind.

assets.title: Coastal Scout
assets.subtitle: Eyes Along Nearchus' Shore
assets.bodyText: A coastal scout studies headlands, landing places, and signs of fresh water ahead of the ships. Alert observation gives the fleet its next safe pause, making unfamiliar coastline a place it can approach.
assets.sceneBrief: A coastal scout studies headland landmarks from a low ancient ship, holds a simple wax note tablet, practical tunic and cloak.

assets.title: Pilot of the Indus Fleet
assets.subtitle: Guide of Nearchus' Passage
assets.bodyText: A fleet pilot weighs currents, shoals, and the shape of the coast before setting a course. Seasoned judgment turns uncertain water into a passage others can follow, protecting the expedition when confidence alone would fail.
assets.sceneBrief: An experienced ancient fleet pilot compares a coastal sketch with the ship's bearing and distant shore, no magnetic compass or modern nautical tools.

assets.title: Navigator of Nearchus
assets.subtitle: Right Hand of the Admiral
assets.bodyText: A senior navigator joins pilots' reports, coastal knowledge, and the needs of the whole fleet. Responsibility reaches beyond one ship, helping Nearchus carry an exhausted expedition through the last demanding miles of its voyage.

assets.title: Eumenes of Cardia
assets.subtitle: Secretary and Strategist
assets.bodyText: Eumenes served Philip II and Alexander as a royal secretary before becoming a commander in the wars of the Successors. His career joined administrative skill to striking victories amid the struggle for Alexander's inheritance.

sources.title: Eumenes of Cardia — Oxford Classical Dictionary

assets.title: Archive Attendant
assets.subtitle: Keeper of the Ordered Shelves
assets.bodyText: An archive attendant sorts bundles and returns each document to the place where it can be found. Quiet order gives the royal office a dependable memory, saving crucial words from the confusion of a crowded day.
assets.sceneBrief: A humble archive attendant orders tied papyrus scroll bundles on wooden shelves in a Macedonian royal office, plain tunic and attentive expression.

assets.title: Royal Dispatch Copyist
assets.subtitle: Scribe in Eumenes' Service
assets.bodyText: A dispatch copyist preserves the wording of orders before they travel far from court. Exact attention keeps authority from changing with each retelling, giving officials a shared instruction they can read and answer.
assets.sceneBrief: A royal dispatch copyist uses a reed pen to copy a letter beside a sealed roll at a modest royal-office desk; no quill pen.

assets.title: Campaign Correspondent
assets.subtitle: Voice Across Eumenes' Lines
assets.bodyText: A campaign correspondent compares dispatches with the movement of forces and the needs of command. Clear writing draws scattered events into focus, allowing distant officers to act with a better understanding of one another.
assets.sceneBrief: A campaign correspondent compares a simple map and multiple dispatches at a field desk, practical cloak and reed pen, camp visible beyond.

assets.title: Secretary of Eumenes
assets.subtitle: Trusted Hand of the Strategist
assets.bodyText: A senior secretary turns reports and decisions into a record command can rely upon. Discretion, precision, and judgment give Eumenes a trusted hand, preserving the intent that holds an army's separate actions together.
